The official Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard scores agent and model configurations on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 dataset, whose task set is the repository release tag v4.0.0 and the Harbor Hub dataset terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0.

On 2026-09-27, EvalRank's exact-byte probe of the anonymous leaderboard-read response for board terminal-bench/terminal-bench 4-0-0 (SHA-256 293e2aaec553a10dba5d12d0cbaebfdcbadfaa274569206dfdee40046cfed62a) found 27 display rows scoring dataset version 1922072f-a433-429a-8929-350d5e1bcf02, each with 330 trials over the 66 tasks at repository commit 452bf305c6daa62fc59061d22133a7cbc7c1572e, and every reported accuracy equal to its successes over trials. No row links a pull request and the repository holds no result submissions, so the adapter reads the board alone.

AA-Omniscience asks 6,000 questions across 42 topics in six domains and reports the Omniscience Index, a bounded -100 to 100 score where higher is better: it rewards correct answers, penalizes incorrect guesses, and keeps abstentions neutral, so 0 means a model answers correctly as often as incorrectly. An LLM grader labels each answer CORRECT, INCORRECT, PARTIAL_ANSWER, or NOT_ATTEMPTED.

The Benchmark Heaven public API serves read-only, CORS-open JSON observations for the registry id aa-omniscience::snapshot-2026-09-10 (its versioned id for the AA-Omniscience Index). Every observation carries the Artificial Analysis source URL, a retrieved_at timestamp and a sha256 of the retrieved source. On 2026-09-29 the API held 538 observations for that snapshot, retrieved from 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-22, covering Claude Opus 5.5 (46.4 at max effort), GPT-6 Astra (43.4 at max, 43.7 at high), Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3; Gemini 2.5 Pro scores -16.4.

Each observation is one model at a named reasoning effort answering Artificial Analysis's fixed prompts, so it resolves to a model configuration under direct prompting and joins the existing factuality and general-knowledge-qa model-configuration ranking groups; no new group is needed. The calibrated-abstention scoring penalizes confident hallucination, which is why the family belongs in factuality as well as general-knowledge-qa. On 2026-09-29 factuality's two boards (FACTS Grounding v2 and Vectara HHEM) overlapped on only 9 models, so a third board widens the cell's two-board coverage floor. No other catalog family shares its questions, so its correlation stays unknown.
